headline: No county publishes whether lung-cancer patients start treatment within six weeks of referral. That missing Goal 3 clock is why Tasan exists — the centrepiece is the waiting-time tracker with a day-28 alert and nurse navigator.
gap: Age-adjusted share of lung cancer patients with curative treatment within 12 months. Men: Lapland ~16.2% vs Vantaa-Kerava ~29.8%. Women: ~23.1% vs ~39.7%
where_in_pathway: Goal 3 asks whether patients start treatment within target timeframes. Target per THL Ohjaus 21/2016 (marked outdated; no lung-specific limit; new cancer-specific targets due 2026-28, roadmap 3.1.2). Day-28 alert and 80% goal are Tasan design choices. No public county statistic reports 6-week compliance. The published times start at diagnosis, cover only five collaborative areas, and only patients who received that treatment within six months.
what_to_do: Lead with T3: Tasan clock: county lung-cancer waiting-time tracker with a day-28 alert and a named nurse navigator who acts on it (pilot: Kymenlaakso and Lapland (one per collaborative area); scalable to all 22 areas). When the day-28 alert fires, the nurse navigator triggers T1 Close the missing step in Kymenlaakso's lung pathway: week-1 pathway map, then 3-day CT, reflex biomarkers and pre-agreed HUS surgery slots where missing (pilot: Kymenlaakso (Kymenhva; Etelä-Suomi collaborative area)) and T2 Every new Lapland lung cancer reviewed by the existing OYS lung-cancer MDT (by video), plus shared access to curative radiotherapy at OYS (RT referral, travel and accommodation, SBRT/chemoradiation slots) (pilot: Lapland (Lapin hyvinvointialue; Pohjois-Suomi collaborative area)).
tasan_clock_note: Target per THL Ohjaus 21/2016 (marked outdated; no lung-specific limit; new cancer-specific targets due 2026-28, roadmap 3.1.2). Day-28 alert and 80% goal are Tasan design choices.
